title: Deep sleep, and the one who sees
hookLine: deep, dreamless sleep seems like the answer, until Indra notices that nobody is home there; after a hundred and one years, Prajapati finally says it
carry: the one who sees through the eye
tomorrow: the horse sacrifice as the cosmos
last: INDRA RETURNS — THE SELF IS THE SELF IS NOT THE DREAMERER.

cards: The best sleep of your life. No alarm, no dreams, nothing at all, and you wake up feeling completely new. Ask where you were during those hours, and the answer is: nowhere.
I was out. And yet something got you safely from night to morning. Indra has now spent sixty-four years with his teacher.
The reflection wasn't the self. The dreamer wasn't the self. So Prajapati tries the deepest rest there is.

teach.b: After another thirty-two years, Prajapati says: when someone is fast asleep, completely at peace, and knows no dream, that is the self. Immortal, fearless. That is Brahman.
Indra leaves content, and on the road the doubt comes a third time. In deep sleep, he doesn't know himself as I am this. He doesn't know these beings.
It's as if he's been wiped out. I see nothing good in this. Back he goes.
This time Prajapati says: live here five more years. Add them up: thirty-two, thirty-two, thirty-two, and five.
A hundred and one years. Then, finally, Prajapati speaks plainly.

teach.h: THE BODY IS MORTAL; IT IS NOT.
teach.b: This body is mortal, gripped by death. But it's the dwelling of a self that is deathless and has no body. While you're tied to the body, pleasure and pain hold you.
Pleasure and pain don't touch what has no body. Then the line our carry comes from. When the eye looks out into space, the one who is there is the person in the eye.
The eye is just for seeing. The one who knows, let me smell this, is the self; the nose is for smelling. Let me speak: speech is for speaking.
Let me hear: the ear is for hearing. Let me think: the mind is its divine eye. Look at the journey.
Not the reflection, which is seen. Not the dreamer, who suffers. Not deep sleep, where nobody's home.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO SEES THROUGH THE EYE.
teach.b: The self is the one who sees through the eye, hears through the ear, thinks through the mind. You never see it, because it's always the one seeing.
This is the atman, the self at the heart of Hindu teaching: there in waking, in dream and in deep sleep, aware of all three. Later Vedanta teachers call it the sakshi, the witness.

how: Many Vedanta teachers end their teaching of the Chandogya with Prajapati's instruction to Indra, and the inquiry into the seer behind the senses is central to Hindu contemplative practice, including the modern self-inquiry taught by Ramana Maharshi.

o: Indra settles on deep sleep as the true self
Indra's third trip back, until the self is the seer
Indra goes home to rule the gods in peace

games.q: Indra's four answers — tap the pairs.
p: the eye is just for seeing

s: Indra studies with Prajapati for a hundred and one years in all
Prajapati says deep sleep is the final answer
Indra finds its flaw: there, he doesn't know himself or anything.
Prajapati calls the mind the self's divine eye
the eye is for seeing, the nose for smelling, and the mind is its divine eye.

games.q: you're Indra. Prajapati says deep, dreamless sleep is the self. on the road, what's your doubt?
o: in deep sleep, I don't know myself or anything; it's as if I'm wiped out.
deep sleep is only for the gods.
games.why: he returns a third time. after five more years, Prajapati speaks plainly: the self is the one who sees through the eye.

practice: Sit with your eyes open, softly, and look at something in front of you: the eye is for seeing, and there's the one who sees. Listen to a sound, then notice a thought, and each time notice the one who hears, the one aware.
Don't try to find that one; just rest as it.

wordCard.voice: Indra returns again. Not the reflection, not the dreamer, not deep sleep. After a hundred and one years: the self is the one who sees through the eye.

orig.note: Sanskrit suṣupti: deep, dreamless sleep. the third state Indra tests.

carryVoice: Your line: the one who sees through the eye. Tomorrow, a new Upanishad opens with a horse. Day three hundred fifty-nine, done.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 8.11.1–3 (deep sleep; five more years)
Chandogya Upanishad 8.12.1–6 (the body mortal, the self bodiless; the eye is for seeing; the mind its divine eye)
